title: 三字经
source: Text: ctext.org (Wang Yinglin, standard 1068-character edition) · Classical translation: Herbert Giles (1900), public domain · Modern interpretation written for this app

couplets.en: Men at their birth are naturally good.
couplets.mod: People are born good at heart.

couplets.en: Their natures are much the same; their habits become widely different.
couplets.mod: Our natures start out alike; it's habit that pulls us apart.

couplets.en: If foolishly there is no teaching, the nature will deteriorate.
couplets.mod: Without teaching, that good nature drifts away.

couplets.en: The right way in teaching is to attach the utmost importance in thoroughness.
couplets.mod: The key to teaching well is focus.

couplets.en: Of old, the mother of Mencius chose a neighbourhood;
couplets.mod: Long ago, Mencius' mother moved house to find her son better neighbors —

couplets.en: and when her child would not learn, she broke the shuttle from the loom.
couplets.mod: and when he slacked off, she cut the cloth on her loom to show him what quitting wastes.

couplets.en: Dou of the Swallow Hills had the right method.
couplets.mod: Dou Yanshan had the right method:

couplets.en: He taught five sons, each of whom raised the family reputation.
couplets.mod: he taught his five sons well, and every one of them made the family name.

couplets.en: To feed without teaching is the father's fault.
couplets.mod: Raising a child without teaching them is the father's failure;

couplets.en: To teach without severity is the teacher's laziness.
couplets.mod: teaching without rigor is the teacher's laziness.

couplets.en: If the child does not learn, this is not as it should be.
couplets.mod: A child who won't learn — that's just not acceptable:

couplets.en: If he does not learn while young, what will he be when old?
couplets.mod: skip learning while young, and what will you be when you're old?

couplets.en: If jade is not polished, it cannot become a thing of use.
couplets.mod: Uncut jade is just a rock;

couplets.en: If a man does not learn, he cannot know his duty towards his neighbour.
couplets.mod: an untaught person never learns what's right.

couplets.en: He who is the son of a man, when he is young
couplets.mod: While you're still young,

couplets.en: should attach himself to his teachers and friends, and practise ceremonial usages.
couplets.mod: stay close to good teachers and friends, and learn how to carry yourself.

couplets.en: Xiang, at nine years of age, could warm (his parents') bed.
couplets.mod: Xiang, aged nine, warmed his parents' bed on winter nights —

couplets.en: Filial piety towards parents, is that to which we should hold fast.
couplets.mod: looking after your parents is the duty to hold onto.

couplets.en: Rong, at four years of age, could yield the (bigger) pears.
couplets.mod: Rong, aged four, passed the bigger pears to his brothers —

couplets.en: To behave as a younger brother towards elders, is one of the first things to know.
couplets.mod: deference to elders is one of the first things to learn.

couplets.en: Begin with filial piety and fraternal love, and then see and hear.
couplets.mod: Family duty comes first; knowledge second:

couplets.en: Learn to count, and learn to read.
couplets.mod: learn your numbers, then learn to read.

couplets.en: Units and tens, tens and hundreds,
couplets.mod: Ones become tens, tens become hundreds,

couplets.en: hundreds and thousands, thousands and tens of thousands.
couplets.mod: hundreds become thousands, thousands become ten-thousands.

couplets.en: The Three Forces are Heaven, Earth and Man.
couplets.mod: The Three Forces: heaven, earth, and people.

couplets.en: The Three Luminaries are the sun, the moon and the stars.
couplets.mod: The Three Lights: sun, moon, and stars.

couplets.en: The Three Bonds are the obligation between sovereign and subject,
couplets.mod: The Three Bonds: ruler and minister bound by duty,

couplets.en: the love between father and child, the harmony between husband and wife.
couplets.mod: parent and child by love, husband and wife by harmony.

couplets.en: We speak of spring and summer, we speak of autumn and winter.
couplets.mod: Spring and summer, autumn and winter —

couplets.en: These four seasons revolve without ceasing.
couplets.mod: the four seasons cycle without end.

couplets.en: We speak of North and South, we speak of East and West,
couplets.mod: South and north, west and east —

couplets.en: These four points respond to the requirements of the centre.
couplets.mod: the four directions, all anchored to the center.

couplets.en: We speak of water, fire, wood, metal and earth.
couplets.mod: Water, fire, wood, metal, earth —

couplets.en: These five elements have their origin in number.
couplets.mod: the Five Elements, rooted in number.

couplets.en: We speak of charity of heart and of duty towards one's neighbour, of propriety, of wisdom, and of truth.
couplets.mod: Kindness, justice, courtesy, wisdom, honesty —

couplets.en: These five virtues admit of no compromise.
couplets.mod: the Five Virtues, and none of them is optional.

couplets.en: Rice, spiked millet, pulse, wheat, glutinous millet and common millet.
couplets.mod: Rice, millet, beans, wheat, and the sticky and common millets —

couplets.en: These six grains are those which men eat.
couplets.mod: the six grains people eat.

couplets.en: The horse, the ox, the sheep, the fowl, the dog, the pig.
couplets.mod: Horse, ox, sheep, chicken, dog, pig —

couplets.en: These six animals, are those which men keep.
couplets.mod: the six animals people raise.

couplets.en: We speak of joy, of anger, we speak of pity, of fear,
couplets.mod: Joy and anger, grief and fear,

couplets.en: of love, of hate, and of desire. These are the seven passions.
couplets.mod: love, hate, desire — the seven emotions everyone carries.

couplets.en: The gourd, earthenware, skin, wood, stone, metal,
couplets.mod: Gourd, clay, hide, wood, stone, metal,

couplets.en: silk, and bamboo, yield the eight musical sounds.
couplets.mod: silk and bamboo — the eight materials instruments are made from.

couplets.en: Great great grandfather, great grandfather, grandfather, father and self,
couplets.mod: Great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, grandfather, father, you,

couplets.en: self and son, son and grandson,
couplets.mod: then your son, your grandson,

couplets.en: from son and grandson on to great grandson and great great grandson.
couplets.mod: and on down to great- and great-great-grandsons:

couplets.en: These are the nine agnates, constituting the kinships of man.
couplets.mod: nine generations — the human family line.

couplets.en: Affection between father and child, harmony between husband and wife,
couplets.mod: Kindness between parent and child, accord between husband and wife,

couplets.en: friendliness on the part of elder brothers, respectfulness on the part of younger brothers,
couplets.mod: older siblings generous, younger ones respectful,

couplets.en: precedence between elders and youngers, as between friend and friend,
couplets.mod: elders and juniors keeping their order, friends staying true,

couplets.en: respect on the part of the sovereign, loyalty on the part of the subject.
couplets.mod: rulers respectful, ministers loyal —

couplets.en: These ten obligations, are common to all men.
couplets.mod: ten duties everyone shares.

couplets.en: In the education of the young, there should be explanation and elucidation,
couplets.mod: Teaching beginners takes real care:

couplets.en: careful teaching of the interpretations of commentators, and due attention to paragraphs and sentences.
couplets.mod: explain every gloss, mark every sentence break.

couplets.en: Those who are learners, must have a beginning.
couplets.mod: Every student needs a starting point:

couplets.en: The "little learning" finished, they proceed to the four books.
couplets.mod: finish the primer, then move on to the Four Books.

couplets.en: There is the Lun Yu, in twenty sections.
couplets.mod: The Analects: twenty chapters

couplets.en: In this, the various disciples have recorded the wise sayings of Confucius.
couplets.mod: of Confucius' sayings, written down by his students.

couplets.en: The works of Mencius are comprised in seven sections.
couplets.mod: Mencius: seven chapters

couplets.en: These explain the way and the exemplification thereof, and expound charity and duty towards one's neighbour.
couplets.mod: on virtue, kindness, and doing right.

couplets.en: The Zhong Yong was written by the pen of Zi-si;
couplets.mod: The Doctrine of the Mean, from Zisi's pen:

couplets.en: Zhong (the middle) being that which does not lean towards any side, Yong (the course) being that which cannot be changed.
couplets.mod: 'the mean' leans to no side; 'the constant' never changes.

couplets.en: He who wrote The Great Learning was the philosopher Zeng.
couplets.mod: The Great Learning, by Master Zeng:

couplets.en: Beginning with cultivation of the individual and ordering of the family, it goes on to government of one's own State and ordering of the Empire.
couplets.mod: from improving yourself and your household to governing a state at peace.

couplets.en: When the Classic of Filial Piety is mastered, and the "Four books" are known by heart,
couplets.mod: With the Classic of Filial Piety mastered and the Four Books by heart,

couplets.en: the next step is to the "Six classics", which may now be studied.
couplets.mod: you're ready to start the Six Classics.

couplets.en: The Books of Poetry, of History and of Changes. The Rites of the Zhou Dynasty, the Book of Rites, and the Spring and Autumn Annals,
couplets.mod: Poetry, History, Changes, the Rites of Zhou, the Book of Rites, Spring and Autumn —

couplets.en: are called the Six Classics, which should be carefully explained and analysed.
couplets.mod: the Six Classics, to be studied and picked apart.

couplets.en: There is the Lian Shan system, there is the Gui Zang,
couplets.mod: There's the Lianshan, the Guicang,

couplets.en: And there is the system of Changes of the Zhou Dynasty; such are the three systems which elucidate the Changes.
couplets.mod: and the Zhou Changes — three systems explaining the Book of Changes.

couplets.en: There are the Regulations, the Counsels, the Instructions, the Announcements,
couplets.mod: Regulations and counsels, instructions and announcements,

couplets.en: the Oaths, the Charges; these are the profundities of the Book of History.
couplets.mod: oaths and charges — the deep layers of the Book of History.

couplets.en: Our Duke of Zhou drew up the Ritual of the Zhou Dynasty,
couplets.mod: Our Duke of Zhou wrote the Rites of Zhou,

couplets.en: in which he set forth the duties of the six classes of officials; and thus gave a settled form to the government.
couplets.mod: set out the six ministries, and gave government its shape.

couplets.en: The Elder and the Younger Dai wrote commentaries on the Book of Rites.
couplets.mod: The two Dais annotated the Book of Rites:

couplets.en: They published the holy words, and Ceremonies and Music were set in order.
couplets.mod: the sages' words preserved, ritual and music complete.

couplets.en: We speak of the Guo Feng, we speak of the Ya and the Song.
couplets.mod: Folk songs, court odes, and hymns —

couplets.en: These are the four sections of the Book of poetry, which should be hummed over and over.
couplets.mod: the four parts of the Book of Poetry, meant to be recited aloud.

couplets.en: When odes ceased to be made, the Spring and Autumn Annals were produced.
couplets.mod: When poetry fell silent, the Spring and Autumn Annals took over,

couplets.en: These Annals contain praise and blame, and distinguish the good from the bad.
couplets.mod: handing out praise and blame, sorting good from bad.

couplets.en: The three commentaries upon the above include that of Gong-Yang,
couplets.mod: Three commentaries unpack it: Gongyang's,

couplets.en: that of Zuo and that of Gu-Liang.
couplets.mod: Zuo's, and Guliang's.

couplets.en: When the Classics are understood, then the writings of the various philosophers should be read.
couplets.mod: Once the Classics are clear, read the philosophers:

couplets.en: Pick out the important points in each, and take a note of all facts.
couplets.mod: pull out their key points, note down the facts.

couplets.en: The five chief philosophers are Xun, Yang,
couplets.mod: The five masters: Xunzi, Yangzi,

couplets.en: Wenzhongzi, Laozi and Zhuangzi.
couplets.mod: Wenzhongzi, Laozi, and Zhuangzi.

couplets.en: When the Classics and the Philosophers are mastered, the various histories should be read,
couplets.mod: Classics and philosophers done, read the histories:

couplets.en: and the genealogical connections should be examined, so that the end of one dynasty and the beginning of the next may be known.
couplets.mod: trace the dynastic lines, learn how each began and ended.

couplets.en: From Fu Xi and Shen Nong on to the Yellow Emperor,
couplets.mod: From Fuxi and Shennong up to the Yellow Emperor —

couplets.en: these are called the Three Rulers. who lived in the early ages.
couplets.mod: the Three Sovereigns of the earliest age.

couplets.en: Tang and You-Yu are called the two emperors.
couplets.mod: Yao and Shun were the Two Emperors:

couplets.en: They adbicated, one after the other, and theirs was called the Golden Age.
couplets.mod: each handed power to the worthiest, and that was the golden age.

couplets.en: The Xia dynasty has Yu; the Shang dynasty has Tang;
couplets.mod: Xia had Yu, Shang had Tang,

couplets.en: the Zhou dynasty had Wen and Wu; these are called the Three Kings
couplets.mod: Zhou had Wen and Wu — together, the Three Kings.

couplets.en: Under the Xia dynasty the throne was transmitted from father to son, making a family possession of the empire.
couplets.mod: Under Xia the throne became hereditary — the empire a family estate;

couplets.en: After four hundred years, the Imperial sacrifice passed from the House of Xia.
couplets.mod: four hundred years on, Xia's altars fell.

couplets.en: Tang the completer destroyed the Xia Dynasty, and the dynastic title became Shang.
couplets.mod: Tang overthrew Xia and named his dynasty Shang;

couplets.en: The line lasted for six hundred years, ending with Zhou Xin.
couplets.mod: six hundred years, down to the tyrant Zhou Xin's fall.

couplets.en: King Wu of the Zhou Dynasty finally slew Zhou Xin.
couplets.mod: King Wu of Zhou struck the tyrant down;

couplets.en: His own line lasted for eight hundred years; the longest dynasty of all.
couplets.mod: his own line ran eight hundred years — the longest of all.

couplets.en: When the Zhous made tracks eastwards, the feudal bond was slackened;
couplets.mod: When Zhou moved its capital east, royal authority slipped:

couplets.en: the arbitrament of spear and shields prevailed; and peripatetic politicians were held in high esteem.
couplets.mod: weapons ruled the day, and traveling persuaders were the stars.

couplets.en: This period began with the Spring and Autumn Epoch, and ended with that of the Warring States.
couplets.mod: It began with the Spring and Autumn era and ended in the Warring States:

couplets.en: Next, the Five Chieftains domineered, and the Seven Martial States came to the front.
couplets.mod: five hegemons threw their weight around; seven great powers emerged.

couplets.en: Then the House of Qin, descended from the Ying clan, finally united all the states under one sway.
couplets.mod: Then Qin, of the Ying clan, swallowed all the rest —

couplets.en: The throne was transmitted to Er Shi, upon which followed the struggle between the Chu and the Han States.
couplets.mod: two emperors later it collapsed, and Chu fought Han for the prize.

couplets.en: Then Gao Zu arose, and the House of Han was established.
couplets.mod: Gaozu won, and the house of Han was founded;

couplets.en: When we come to the reign of Xiao Ping, Wang Mang usurped the throne.
couplets.mod: by Emperor Ping's day, Wang Mang had stolen the throne.

couplets.en: Then Guang Wu arose, and founded the Eastern Han dynasty.
couplets.mod: Guangwu rose and restored it as the Eastern Han:

couplets.en: It lasted four hundred years, and ended with the Emperor Xian.
couplets.mod: four hundred years in all, ending with Emperor Xian.

couplets.en: Wei, Shu and Wu, fought for the sovereignty of the Hans.
couplets.mod: Wei, Shu, and Wu fought over the Han inheritance —

couplets.en: They were called the Three Kingdoms, and existed until the Two Jin Dynasties.
couplets.mod: the Three Kingdoms, lasting into the two Jins.

couplets.en: Then followed the Song and the Qi dynasties, and after them the Liang and Chen dynasties.
couplets.mod: Song and Qi came next, then Liang and Chen:

couplets.en: These are the Southern dynasties, with their capital at Nanjing.
couplets.mod: the Southern Dynasties, ruling from Nanjing.

couplets.en: The northern dynasties are the Wei dynasty of the Yuan family, which split into Eastern and Western We,.
couplets.mod: In the north, the Tuoba Wei split east and west,

couplets.en: the Zhou dynasty of the Yuwen family, with the Qi dynasty of the Gao family.
couplets.mod: then the Yuwen Zhou and the Gao family's Qi.

couplets.en: At length, under the Sui dynasty, the empire was united under one ruler.
couplets.mod: At last the Sui made the realm one again —

couplets.en: The throne was not transmitted twice, succession to power being lost.
couplets.mod: but couldn't pass the throne on twice before losing it.

couplets.en: The first emperor of the Tang dynasty raised volunteer troops.
couplets.mod: The Tang founder raised a righteous army,

couplets.en: He put an end to the disorder of the House of Sui, and established the foundations of his line.
couplets.mod: ended the Sui chaos, and laid his dynasty's foundations:

couplets.en: Twenty times the thrown was transmitted in a period of three hundred years.
couplets.mod: twenty successions across three hundred years,

couplets.en: The Liang State destroyed it, and the dynastic title was changed.
couplets.mod: until Liang destroyed it and the title changed hands.

couplets.en: The Liang, the Tang, the Jin, the Han, and the Zhou,
couplets.mod: Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, Zhou —

couplets.en: are called the Five Dynasties, and there was a reason for the establishment of each.
couplets.mod: the Five Dynasties, each with its own story.

couplets.en: Then the fire-led house of Song arose, and received the resignation of the house of Zhou.
couplets.mod: Then the fire-crowned Song arose, taking the throne by abdication:

couplets.en: Eighteen times the throne was transmitted, and then the north and the south were reunited.
couplets.mod: eighteen successions, and then north and south merged again.

couplets.en: The Seventeen Dynastic Histories are all embraced in the above.
couplets.mod: The Seventeen Histories — it's all in there:

couplets.en: They contain examples of good and bad government, whence may be learnt the principles of prosperity and decay.
couplets.mod: order and chaos, and why states rise and fall.

couplets.en: Ye who read history must study the State Annals,
couplets.mod: Read history alongside the primary records,

couplets.en: whereby you will understand ancient and modern events, as though having seen them with your own eyes.
couplets.mod: until past and present feel like things you watched yourself.

couplets.en: Recite them with the mouth, and ponder over them in your hearts.
couplets.mod: Recite it aloud, turn it over in your heart —

couplets.en: Do this in the morning; do this in the evening.
couplets.mod: morning and evening, every single day.

couplets.en: Of old, Confucius took Xiang Tuo for his teacher.
couplets.mod: Even Confucius took the boy Xiang Tuo as a teacher;

couplets.en: The inspired men and sages of old studied diligently nevertheless.
couplets.mod: the sages of old never stopped studying.

couplets.en: Zhao, president of the Council, studied the Lu text of the Lun Yu.
couplets.mod: Zhao Pu, already chief minister, still studied his Analects —

couplets.en: He, when already an official, studied, and moreover with diligence.
couplets.mod: in office, and diligent all the same.

couplets.en: One opened out rushes and plaited them together; another scraped tablets of bamboo.
couplets.mod: One man copied books onto woven rushes; another shaved bamboo strips:

couplets.en: These men had no books, but they knew how to make an effort.
couplets.mod: they owned no books, yet made the effort anyway.

couplets.en: One tied his head to the beam above him; another pricked his thigh with an awl.
couplets.mod: One tied his hair to a roof beam to stay awake; another jabbed an awl into his thigh:

couplets.en: They were not taught, but toiled hard of their own accord.
couplets.mod: nobody pushed them — they drove themselves.

couplets.en: Then we have one who put fireflies in a bag. and again another who used the white glare from snow.
couplets.mod: One read by a bag of fireflies, another by the glare off snow:

couplets.en: Although their families were poor, these men studied unceasingly.
couplets.mod: dirt poor, and the studying never stopped.

couplets.en: Again, there was one who carried fuel, and another who used horns as pegs.
couplets.mod: One studied while hauling firewood, another with books hung on an ox horn:

couplets.en: Although they toiled with their bodies, they were nevertheless remarkable for their application.
couplets.mod: worn out by work, they still kept at it.

couplets.en: Su Lao-Quan, at the age of twenty-seven,
couplets.mod: Su Xun was twenty-seven

couplets.en: at last began to show his energy and devote himself to the study of books.
couplets.mod: before he finally got serious and hit the books —

couplets.en: Then when already past the age, he deeply regretted his delay.
couplets.mod: and even old, he regretted starting late.

couplets.en: You little boys should take thought betimes.
couplets.mod: So you who are young: think about it early.

couplets.en: Then there were Liang Hao, who at the age of eighty-two,
couplets.mod: There was Liang Hao, who at eighty-two

couplets.en: made his replies in the great hall, and came out first among many scholars.
couplets.mod: topped the palace examination ahead of a hall full of scholars.

couplets.en: When thus late he had succeeded, all men pronounced him a prodigy.
couplets.mod: A success that late, everyone called a marvel —

couplets.en: You little boys should make up your minds to work.
couplets.mod: so you who are young: set your goal now.

couplets.en: Ying, at eight years of age, could compose poetry.
couplets.mod: Zu Ying at eight could compose poetry;

couplets.en: Bi, at seven years of age, could make an epigram on wei-qi.
couplets.mod: Li Bi at seven wrote verses about the game of go.

couplets.en: These youths were quick of apprehension, and people declared them to be prodigies.
couplets.mod: Quick minds like that were called prodigies —

couplets.en: You young learners ought to imitate them.
couplets.mod: you young learners should measure yourselves against them.

couplets.en: Cai Wen-ji, was able to judge from the sound of a psaltery.
couplets.mod: Cai Wenji could read music by ear;

couplets.en: Xie Dao-yun, was able to compose verses.
couplets.mod: Xie Daoyun improvised verse.

couplets.en: They were only girls, yet they were quick and clever.
couplets.mod: They were girls — and that sharp.

couplets.en: You boys ought to rouse yourselves.
couplets.mod: Boys, consider that your wake-up call.

couplets.en: Liu Yan of the Tang dynasty, when only seven years of age,
couplets.mod: Liu Yan of the Tang, at just seven,

couplets.en: was ranked as an "inspired child," and was appointed a Corrector of Texts.
couplets.mod: was named a child prodigy and given a court post correcting texts.

couplets.en: He, although a child, was already in an official post.
couplets.mod: A child, and already serving in office —

couplets.en: You young learners strive to bring about a like result.
couplets.mod: work at it, and you can get there too:

couplets.en: Those who work will also succeed as he did.
couplets.mod: whoever puts in the effort ends up like him.

couplets.en: The dog keeps guard by night; the cock proclaims the dawn.
couplets.mod: The dog guards the night; the rooster calls the dawn —

couplets.en: If foolishly you do not study, how can you become men?
couplets.mod: if you refuse to learn, how do you deserve to be called a person?

couplets.en: The silkworm produces silk, the bee makes honey.
couplets.mod: The silkworm spins silk; the bee makes honey —

couplets.en: If a man does not learn, he is not equal to the brutes
couplets.mod: a person who won't learn does less than the animals.

couplets.en: Learn while young, and when grown up apply what you have learnt;
couplets.mod: Learn while young, act on it grown:

couplets.en: influencing the sovereign above; benefiting the people below.
couplets.mod: serve the country above, lift the people below.

couplets.en: Make a name for yourselves, and glorify your father and mother,
couplets.mod: Make your name and honor your parents;

couplets.en: shed lustre on your ancestors, enrich your posterity.
couplets.mod: shine credit on your ancestors, leave your children better off.

couplets.en: Men bequeath to their children coffers of gold;
couplets.mod: Others leave their children chests full of gold;

couplets.en: I teach you children only this one book.
couplets.mod: I leave you children just this one book:

couplets.en: Diligence has its reward; play has no advantages.
couplets.mod: hard work pays off; fooling around pays nothing.

couplets.en: Oh, be on your guard, and put forth your strength.
couplets.mod: Be warned — and give it everything.
